chunks: Al-Ṣafwānī said: I heard Abū ‘Alī ibn Himmām say: I heard Muḥammad ibn ‘Alī al-‘Azzāqirī al-Shalmaghānī say:

The Truth is one, but its shirts (garments/cloaks) differ. One day it is in white, one day in red, and one day in blue. Ibn Himmām said: This was the first thing I rejected from his words, because it is the saying of the Ahl al-Ḥulūl (Proponents of Incarnation).

key_terms.قُمُصُهُ: His shirts/garments (metaphor for forms or manifestations)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'changing shirts' metaphor in Shia theological critique of Incarnation?
ai.summary: Muḥammad ibn ‘Alī al-‘Azzāqirī employs the metaphor of changing garments to illustrate the unity of Truth manifesting through diverse forms, a concept central to the Ahl al-Ḥulūl (Proponents of Divine Incarnation). Abū ‘Alī ibn Himmām identifies this specific imagery as the primary doctrinal flaw, marking it as the decisive point for rejecting al-‘Azzāqirī’s claim to deputyship. This critique highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between true divine manifestation and the pantheistic tendency to conflate the Creator with created forms.
